title: Property-Based Testing
concept: Property-based testing verifies that invariants hold for randomly generated inputs — like unit tests on steroids.
why: Instead of testing specific values, you test PROPERTIES that should hold for ALL values. The framework finds counterexamples automatically.
tips: The best properties are simple and universal — they read like mathematical laws
Think about properties BEFORE writing the implementation — they guide the design
Combine property-based testing with contracts — contracts catch bugs, properties verify behavior
Shrinking is magic — it turns a massive failing input into a 2-element counterexample
common_mistakes: Writing properties that are too weak (always true even for buggy implementations)
Testing properties on only the happy path — the framework tests the UNHAPPY path
Writing properties that reimplement the function — `prop: f(x) == f(x)` is a useless tautology
